Remind Me, My Dream

Kelly Strayhorn Theater

5941 Penn Ave · Pittsburgh · East Liberty

Get tickets$0 to %25
Arts & Community: Community

Seventeen AAPI artists from JADED use the creative process to explore layered identities and stories, while making space for dreams, grief, and connection. Through painting, sculpture, sound, film, wood, glass, and textiles, the artists reflect on messages held in their bodies, personal histories, and memories. The exhibition’s opening reception includes a Kintsugi Grief Bowls workshop with artist Kiyomi Knox, which uses the Japanese practice of repairing broken pottery with gold to symbolize the beauty that can exist in brokenness. Performing artist Arieux meditates on death, loss, and grief with a procession inspired by the ancient Chinese profession of corpse walkers. Remind Me, My Dream features works by Arieux, Anne Chen, Shimul Chowdhury, Sara Dtantirojanarat, Eriko Hattori, Sarah Khadraoui, Kiyomi Knox, Jules Lee, Justin Lin, Arthur Lindsay, Brent Nakamoto, Quartz/Court, Kimberly Rooney 高小荣, SEONI, Becky Sungja Kim, Zim Syed, and Zoyakeko. Led by women and non-binary artists, JADED is Pittsburgh’s first AAPI artist collective celebrating AAPI art & culture in Pittsburgh. Remind Me, My Dream is curated by Sara Tang in partnership with JADED and commissioned by KST in conjunction with Maree ReMalia’s WITH OURSELVES, WITH EACH OTHER.

WPSD: A Night at the Museum - Auction and Fundraiser

Mattress Factory Contemporary Art Museum

509 Jacksonia Street · Pittsburgh · North Side

Get tickets150.00
Arts & Community: Fundraisers

Think of our "A Night at the Museum: Auction & Reception" as a gala-lite. There will be plenty of hors d'oeuvres, an open bar, and silent auction items just like many of our Fall events. You'll also be able to browse all of the cool, quirky, and artsy exhibits - complete with attendants and ASL interpreters on every floor of the museum. We'll also have live music and a live painter (artist Phil Seth) to liven up the evening. About our Venue: The Mattress Factory is a contemporary art museum located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was a pioneer of site-specific installation art and features permanent installations by artists Yayoi Kusama, James Turrell, and Greer Lankton. The museum's roof itself is a light art installation and part of Pittsburgh's Northside evening skyline. Barbara Luderowski purchased a derelict Stearns & Foster mattress warehouse in 1975. The museum achieved non-profit status in 1977. Over the next forty years, Luderowski would attract upcoming installation artists to fill its rooms. The Mattress Factory along with its neighbors City of Asylum and Randyland are credited with playing a role in Pittsburgh's revitalization. (SOURCE: Wikipedia)

Textures of Being Community Forum

Contemporary Craft

5645 Butler Street · Pittsburgh · Lawrenceville

Get tickets$20 ($12 for students), registration required.
Arts & Community: CommunityArts & Community: Exhibits

Textures of Being Forum is an intimate, daylong program centered on disability, accessibility, the body, and artistic practice. Textures of Being Community Forum is an intimate, daylong program presented through a collaboration between Contemporary Craft and Anthropology of Motherhood. Centered on disability, accessibility, the body, and artistic practice, the forum brings together artists, advocates, and cultural leaders to consider how access shapes the ways we communicate, create, organize, and participate in community life. The program will feature three complementary presentations. Artist and self-advocate Mark Steidl will address creative voice, communication, and the importance of disabled people telling their own stories. Kristen Link of The Woodlands Foundation will discuss how organizations can move beyond individual accommodations to build sustained cultures of access and belonging. Artists from the Anthropology of Motherhood: Deaf & Disability Art Exhibition will share how Deaf and disability culture, caregiving, embodiment, and access inform their artistic processes and relationships with audiences. Through presentations, facilitated conversation, and an interactive “Cards for Inclusion” activity, participants will explore accessibility not as an afterthought, but as a creative, relational, and institutional practice. The forum is designed for a small group of approximately 25 participants, allowing space for meaningful dialogue, shared learning, and connection. 1. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation will be provided at this program. 2. If you require accommodation to fully participate in this activity, please indicate in the registration form. Accommodations for individuals will be reviewed/provided at least an 15-day advance notice. Thank you! 3. Lunch in buffet style will be provided for this event. Please indicate any dietary restrictions in the registration form.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Ten Evenings: Michael Lewis

Carnegie Music Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh · Oakland

Get tickets$30.94 to $42.14
Arts & Community: LectureArts & Community: Literary

An inside look at the early days of Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency, as told by the public servants it targeted and one of America’s best storytellers. Blockers. It wasn’t a compliment. In the new Washington, it was the worst thing you could be—especially if you worked in the federal government and wanted to keep your job. A Blocker was a holdover, an impediment, someone who didn’t get the message—and, most of all, someone who didn’t belong. Michael Lewis found seven of them. Blockers is the story of people who believed they had a calling, who were convinced they were doing something the country couldn’t do without, and then discovered they were no longer wanted. One kept Americans’ most sensitive tax data out of the wrong hands and another made sure that politicians and civil servants played by the rules. One figured out how to stop wildfires from destroying suburban neighborhoods, another helped uncover the mysteries of cystic fibrosis. There was also a security guard. It should come as no surprise that the writer who made subprime mortgages gripping (The Big Short) and who turned baseball statistics into poetry (Moneyball) could transform the first two years of the second Trump administration into a thriller about federal employees. But he does. And he does something else. He puts before us a clear question: If these public servants can’t survive in government today, then what does that say about us? New York Times bestselling author Michael Lewis has published many books on subjects ranging from politics to Wall Street. Lewis’s most recent #1 New York Times bestselling book, Going Infinite, tells the story of FTX’s collapse and the enigmatic founder at its center, Sam Bankman-Fried. Lewis is the creator and host of Apple’s #1 rated podcast Against the Rules, a searing look at what’s happened to fairness in American life through the lens of people who depend on public trust. Mr. Lewis grew up in New Orleans and remains deeply interested and involved in the city. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Art History from Princeton and a Master’s degree in Economics from the London School of Economics. He lives in Berkeley, California, with his wife, Tabitha Soren, and their children.

Elanor Moss

The Funhouse @ Mr. Smalls

400 Lincoln Ave · Millvale

Get ticketsADV: $15 / DOS: $18
Music: Acoustic

Mr. Smalls Presents Elanor Moss Doors: 7:00 pm / Show: 8:00 pm London-based songwriter Elanor Moss announces her signing to Merge Records and releases the new single, “Again, My Love.” The release follows 2025 tours with Foxwarren, Flyte, and Ye Vagabonds, and was met with support across the UK, with BBC6 Music naming her “One To Watch 2026” Elanor Moss grew up in a very creative, devoutly Catholic family, and began playing music at church events. Homeschooled through early youth, her parents put a real emphasis on nature and reading and music. Eventually leaving the faith, Moss started writing songs of her own in York as a student of English literature and playing open mics around the city. While at University she also discovered songwriting greats: Leonard Cohen, Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, The Beatles. Shortly after graduation, Moss met producer Oli Deakin, who offered to record her first EP, “Citrus.” Her work with Deakin took her to New York City, where she began forging a sense of community. Between “Citrus” and her second EP, “Cosmic,” Moss toured with Christian Lee Hutson, Benjamin Francis Leftwich and LYR, played one-off shows with Cassandra Jenkins, CMAT, and Sam Amidon, and performed at Pitchfork London, Green Man Festival, and Mosely Folk, among others. DBT Therapy Group

Online

Get ticketsFree
Arts & Community: Community

A skills-based DBT group for adults working on emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Dialectical Behavior Therapy teaches concrete tools for managing intense emotions, sitting with discomfort without acting on it, and communicating needs in relationships without escalating conflict. The group is facilitated by a licensed clinician at Darin King Counseling, a trauma-informed practice in downtown Pittsburgh. Sessions are structured around skills practice rather than open-ended discussion, so participants leave with something they can use that week. Group therapy is not a substitute for individual treatment, and a brief screening call is required before joining to make sure the group is a good fit. Space is limited. To ask questions or reserve a spot, call (724) 268-0223 or visit darinkingcounselingllc.com.

Barbara Kingsolver in conversation with Anna Singer

Carnegie Music Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$39 to $70
Arts & Community: LectureArts & Community: Literary

The story of a brief, passionate, life-changing love affair, wrapped up in what might be the greatest romance of all: our eternal human longing for art and beauty. Livia Cable has made her peace with her marriage and modest livelihood in the farm country where she grew up, until a shocking phone call from an old lover shakes her to the core. Decades earlier, this man knew her as Livia Bohusz, a music conservatory student estranged from her home and family, uncertain of anything except her passion for music and promise as an extraordinary pianist. His request, now, to see her again stirs up ghosts she’s kept at bay for a lifetime. Shifting between past and present, Livia’s decision to meet or reject the reunion means confronting step by step, in memories framed as musical dances, the experiences of childhood loss, abandonment, self-immolating passion, and perilous attachment to a man who broke her belief in love and ruptured the course of her life. With razor-sharp acuity and deep affection, Pulitzer Prize winner Barbara Kingsolver’s unforgettable new novel reflects on class barriers, the risks of ambition, and the timeless, life-changing power of art. Barbara Kingsolver is the author of ten bestselling works of fiction, including the novels Unsheltered, The Bean Trees, and The Poisonwood Bible, as well as books of poetry, essays, creative nonfiction, and Coyote’s Wild Home, a children’s book co-authored with Lily Kingsolver. She also collaborated with family members on the influential Animal, Vegetable, Miracle: A Year of Food Life. Kingsolver’s work has been translated into more than thirty languages and has earned a devoted readership at home and abroad. She is a member of the American Academy of Arts and Letters, and has received numerous awards and honors including the 2023 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for her novel, Demon Copperhead, the National Humanities Medal, and most recently, the National Book Foundation’s Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters. She lives with her husband on a farm in southern Appalachia.

The Artist and the Apparition: Vanka’s Murals and the Cultural Value of Ghost Stories

St. Nicholas Croatian Catholic Church

24 Maryland Avenue · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$20
Arts & Community: TalkArts & Community: Visual Art

American folklore is full of ghost stories—tales and legends passed down from generation to generation. As Maxo Vanka worked on the murals at St Nicholas Croatian Catholic Church, he once remarked to a friend that he saw something “terribly strange.” Vanka did not share his ghost story in public as it would be considered culturally taboo. In many different cultures, tales of ghosts are meant to remain unsaid. But, now Maxo Vanka’s ghost story is being shared with the Millvale community. In “The Artist and The Apparition,” you’ll learn the cultural role of ghost stories within immigrant communities, and how this ghost story is tied with the creation of Vanka’s 1937 murals. Join Vanka Murals Tour docent Timothy R. Grieve-Carlson, an assistant professor of Religion at Westminster College, for a special tour, The Artist and The Apparition, on October 29, 2026 from 6:30 pm - 7:30 pm.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Arcade Comedy Theater

Join us for a hilarious night of anecdotes and improv provided by storytellers and performers who have two things in common: each is UNIQUE, and they all have disabilities! Featuring monologists recruited from the disability and mental health community who share real stories about their lives and a cast of improvisers with disabilities ranging from: stuttering disorders, autism, PTSD, ADHD, anxiety disorders, depression, and many others! 1:00 PM

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

A skills-based DBT group for adults working on emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Dialectical Behavior Therapy teaches concrete tools for managing intense emotions, sitting with discomfort without acting on it, and communicating needs in relationships without escalating conflict. The group is facilitated by a licensed clinician at Darin King Counseling, a trauma-informed practice in downtown Pittsburgh. Sessions are structured around skills practice rather than open-ended discussion, so participants leave with something they can use that week. "Out of Body" Art Exhibition Opening

Irma Freeman Center for Imagination

5006 Penn Ave. · Pittsburgh · Garfield

free
Arts & Community: Visual ArtMusic: Indie

In November of 2026, Irma Freeman Center for Imagination will be presenting a special project organized by artist Tom Sarver. Out of Body is a show of four Pittsburgh artists who approach the title theme from different directions. Maritza Mosquera creates visceral images that allude to one’s inner and outer connection to living, both physically and spiritually. Sarah Zeffiro creates large-scale abstract paintings that push the physicality of art making with the joy and exuberance of mark and symbol. Tom Sarver delves deep into the mind to render images of Pittsburgh arts experiences in specific time and place. David Montano’s conceptual approach often begins with the finding of a cherished artifact of the past, then responding with a work that contemplates the life of the original owner. Out of Body has roots in the recent publication, Pittsburgh’s Avant-Garde: 60 Years Inside the Underground Art Scene, by Sheila Ali, which featured work by Sarver and Zeffiro. It continues the avant-garde spirit of that project and brings new voices, Montano and Mosquera, into the conversation. A tribute to Sheila Ali, longtime curator and director of programs at the Irma Freeman Center of Imagination, will be part of the exhibition. The exhibition opens Friday, November 6th, 6PM - 9PM, during Unblurred, First Fridays on Penn Avenue. There will be a performance by the band "Cisco Kid" during the ceremony. The exhibition closes December 4th.

6:00 PM

Ami Taf Ra & Kamasi Washington presenting The Prophet & The Madman

City Winery Pittsburgh

1627 Smallman Street · Pittsburgh · Strip District

66
Music: JazzMusic: Soul

Presented in partnership with City Winery Pittsburgh North African, Los Angeles-based vocalist and composer Ami Taf Ra joins acclaimed saxophonist, composer, and producer Kamasi Washington for a special November 2026 tour presentation celebrating their ongoing creative collaboration and Ami’s debut album, The Prophet and the Madman. Produced by Washington and released through Brainfeeder, The Prophet and the Madman brings together Moroccan Gnawa, Arabic musical traditions, gospel, soul, and spiritual jazz in a deeply personal exploration of duality, healing, ancestral memory, and transformation. Inspired in part by the writings of Lebanese-American poet Kahlil Gibran, the album creates a sweeping musical world in which Ami’s commanding, operatic voice moves between intimacy, theatricality, and spiritual release. Since its release, the album has earned significant critical recognition. The Prophet and the Madman is nominated for Best Spiritual Album at the Libera Awards, and the Ami/Washington collaboration “Gnawa” was named one of NPR’s Best Songs of 2025. Ami Taf Ra was also recognized among Stereogum’s Best New Artists of 2025. The artistic connection between Ami and Washington is at the heart of the project. Their collaboration can be heard on “How I Became a Madman,” a soaring meditation on the tension between inner chaos and clarity, and throughout an album shaped by Washington’s expansive production and Ami’s singular cross-cultural perspective. Together, they create music that feels both ancient and forward-looking, connecting North African and Middle Eastern traditions with the freedom, improvisation, and communal spirit of contemporary jazz. Ami has performed internationally across Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and the United States, including appearances with the Dutch Royal Metropole Orchestra, North Sea Jazz, Blue Note Tokyo, and Ronnie Scott’s in the UK, as well as performances at the Hollywood Bowl Jazz Festival, City Winery Boston, and the Just Jazz Concert Series in Los Angeles. Grammy winning and Emmy nominated composer and saxophonist Kamasi Washington is one of the defining musical voices of his generation, building an expansive body of work that reaches across jazz, soul, hip-hop, classical music, film, and TV. Their November 2026 performances offer audiences a rare opportunity to experience the world of The Prophet and the Madman live, with Ami’s evocative storytelling and extraordinary vocal range meeting the power, imagination, and spiritual intensity of Kamasi Washington’s musical universe.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Signal Otter Films presents Tee Park's Cece's Interlude! We will be at the Mr. Roboto Project on Saturday, November 7. Doors at 7. Show at 8 with a runtime of 100 minutes. Snacks and drinks provided. Masking highly recommended. Suggested donation $12 or pay what you can. Set in Los Angeles - Cece’s Interlude, directed by Tee Park, follows a troubled young mother and an overstepping documentarian. Filmmaker Sophie-Anne documents the daily life of Cece, a transgender girl and content creator who’s pregnant. Facing much scrutiny, Cece is a typical 20 something who likes to party and has little plans for the future, let alone having a baby. Straddling between modes of documentary and satire alongside themes around how media can employ meaning through exploitative practices of storytelling, in addition to blending a narrative toward conversations of bodily autonomy and respectability – ultimately, according to the director, It’s a story about bias, motherhood, and the predatory gaze. It serves as a satire of the media's long standing predatory practice of unfair portrayals of queer subjects.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

A skills-based DBT group for adults working on emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Dialectical Behavior Therapy teaches concrete tools for managing intense emotions, sitting with discomfort without acting on it, and communicating needs in relationships without escalating conflict. The group is facilitated by a licensed clinician at Darin King Counseling, a trauma-informed practice in downtown Pittsburgh. Sessions are structured around skills practice rather than open-ended discussion, so participants leave with something they can use that week. Group therapy is not a substitute for individual treatment, and a brief screening call is required before joining to make sure the group is a good fit. Space is limited. Words & Pictures: Erin Entrada Kelly

Carnegie Library Lecture Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh · Downtown

Get ticketsFree
Arts & Community: KidstuffArts & Community: Literary

Twelve-year-old Zuzu Santos doesn’t want a robot. She and her best friends would rather explore Bright Valley on their own. But then Zuzu meets Snap, a know-it-all guardian robot with a limited battery life and an abundance of hope. A gripping, stand-alone, thematically rich survival story by two-time Newbery Medalist Erin Entrada Kelly, for fans of The Wild Robot and A Rover’s Story. Bright Valley Subsidized Camp #5 is not a perfect place to live. It’s dusty, there are no trees to provide respite from the beating sun, the trailers are falling apart, and the water supply is heavily rationed. But to twelve-year-old Zuzu Santos and her three best friends, Bright Valley is home. When Zuzu’s dad loses his job at Lockwood, the corporation that controls everything from rations to education, he isn’t given money or food or water as severance, but a dated, first-generation robot. They do not provide a working charging station. Zuzu names the robot Snap, and he soon becomes part of the Bright Valley family. But Snap’s battery is dwindling every day, and though Snap is prepared for his inevitable reset, Zuzu isn’t. She would do whatever it takes to keep Snap alive. The problem is, Snap would do the same for Zuzu and her friends, no matter the cost. Erin Entrada Kelly tells a moving story of friendship and family, rich with themes and characters that will resonate with readers. The Second Life of Snap is a futuristic book for middle graders that is grounded, full of heart and humor, and unforgettable. An excellent choice for fans of The Wild Robot, A Rover’s Story, and Erin Entrada Kelly’s own We Dream of Space. Erin Entrada Kelly is the author of the Newbery Medal–winning novels Hello, Universe and The First State of Being, which was also named a finalist for the National Book Award. She received a Newbery Honor for her acclaimed novel We Dream of Space. Erin Entrada Kelly grew up in Lake Charles, Louisiana, and now lives in Delaware. She teaches in the MFA in writing for children and young adults program at Hamline University. Her short fiction has been nominated for the Philippines Free Press Literary Award for Short Fiction and the Pushcart Prize. Before becoming a children’s author, she worked as a journalist and magazine editor and received numerous awards for community service journalism, feature writing, and editing from the Louisiana Press Association and the Associated Press. Erin Entrada Kelly’s debut novel, Blackbird Fly, was a Kirkus Best Book of the Year, a School Library Journal Best Book of the Year, an ALSC Notable Book, and an Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature Honor Book. She is also the author of The Land of Forgotten Girls, winner of the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature; You Go First, an Indie Next Pick; Lalani of the Distant Sea, an Indie Next Pick; Those Kids from Fawn Creek, named to numerous best-of-the-year lists; The Second Life of Snap, which received six starred reviews; and six popular novels for younger readers, Maybe Maybe Marisol Rainey, Surely Surely Marisol Rainey, Only Only Marisol Rainey, Your Turn Marisol Rainey, Felix Powell, Boy Dog, and Felix Powell, Boy Squirrel, which she also illustrated. Erin Entrada Kelly’s acclaimed nonfiction debut, At Last She Stood, was the recipient of the Robert F. Sibert Honor. It tells the sweeping story of Filipino World War II guerrilla fighter Josefina Guerrero.

Member Preview: Greer Lankton: "Could it be Love"

Mattress Factory Contemporary Art Museum

509 Jacksonia St · Pittsburgh · Mexican War Streets

Free for Mattress Factory members
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Greer Lankton: Could It Be Love Curated by Francis Schichtel and Jordan Weitzman Could It Be Love presents an intimate and powerful photographic survey of Greer Lankton (1958–1996), the legendary East Village artist known for her uncannily lifelike dolls and fearless exploration of gender, beauty, and the body. Featuring 24 rarely seen photographs of her iconic dolls, taken by Lankton herself, this exhibition reveals her uncanny ability to imbue life into her sculpted figures as they lounge, gossip, and perform across New York’s gritty and gorgeous downtown scene. This exhibition celebrates Lankton not only as a trailblazing trans artist but also as a completely original image-maker whose lens captured a world of oddballs, queer icons, and doll-like doppelgängers with equal parts glamour, melancholy, and wit. Presented in partnership with Magic Hour Press, Could It Be Love follows the release of the first major monograph on Lankton’s photographic work. Discover the new exhibition, then mingle with fellow members over drinks in the lobby. Not a member yet? Support the museum today and gain access to special events all year long. Please note, parking is limited at our main lot at 505 Jacksonia Street, with additional street parking available in the surrounding neighborhood. About Greer Lankton Greer Lankton (1958 – 1996) was one of the most significant artists to have taken part in the revolutionary art scene of New York City’s East Village during the 1980s. Lankton grew up in Park Forest, IL, where she graduated a year early from high school to attend the Art Institute of Chicago from 1975 to1978. That year she moved to New York City and received her BFA from Pratt Institute in 1981. By then Lankton had secured her reputation as a leading figure in the social ferment of NYC in the 1980s through her visceral doll sculpture, and now lesser-known performances and minimalist soft sculpture. Lankton’s drawings are frequently compared to that of the expressionist Egon Schiele and her dolls and their photographic portraits, to that of surrealist Hans Bellmer. Yet her experimental and multimedia work are located within a history of transfeminism, avant-garde performance and even pop-art, while at the same time is equally situated within a neo-punk canon and the Trash Trilogy of John Waters films - Pink Flamingos being her favorite. Lankton’s exhibitions and performances included those at PS1, Club 57, Pyramid Club, Franklyn Furnace, Civilian Warfare Gallery, Hal Bromm and the Whitney Biennale, NYC. She also exhibited across the US and Europe, including the UK, Austria and the Venice Biennale, Italy. She exhibited her first full-scale installation artwork at the Mattress Factory Museum shortly before her untimely death in 1996. About the monograph Could It Be Love Edited by Nan Goldin, Francis Schichtel, and Jordan Weitzman, the book draws deeply from the Greer Lankton Archive, housed at Mattress Factory, to present over 100 of Lankton’s rarely seen photographs. These images offer an intimate and theatrical glimpse into Lankton’s inner world, one populated by glamorous oddballs, downtown legends, and avatars of her own making. This exhibition is made possible by Teiger Foundation.

Guided Tour: Textures of Being

Contemporary Craft

5645 Butler Street · Pittsburgh · Lawrenceville

Get ticketsFree
Arts & Community: TalkArts & Community: Visual Art

Join us for a guided tour of Textures of Being. Textures of Being brings together artists whose practices honor the body—its sensitivities and its wisdom—as a site of deep creative knowledge. Rooted in materiality and lived experience, this exhibition reimagines disability as a form of freedom and a distinct intimate lens through which the world is encountered, shaped, and perceived. In the United States, one in four adults lives with a disability. Yet our environment and cultural system continue to privilege an imagined norm, often neglecting the rich variation of how bodies move, feel, perceive, and relate. This exhibition shifts the focus from compliance and accommodation to the sensory realities that animate disabled life—textures of resistance and adaptation, fragility and strength, constraint and imagination. Together, the artists create a multidimensional portrait of embodiment that exceeds symbolic inclusion and moves toward a fuller, more tender understanding of what it means to inhabit a body. The intimacy and solidarity expressed through the work evoke a sense of care, reciprocity and community. Textures of Being is both an offering and a call for everyone to honor the textures that make each of us, and all of us, fully and profoundly human. This exhibition was juried and organized by Yu-San Cheng, Director of Visual Engagement at Contemporary Craft, and Fran Flaherty, the creator of Anthropology of Motherhood and a deaf artist based in Pittsburgh.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Scream At Your Demons: A Benefit for Guitars4Vets

The Funhouse @ Mr. Smalls

400 Lincoln Ave · Millvale

Get tickets$20
Arts & Community: FundraisersMusic: Metal

Chaotic Order Entertainment Presents Scream At Your Demons: A Benefit for Guitars4Vets Featuring: Desolence Lyssa Quell Lysandra Feast On The Fallen Fall Off The Earth and more TBA! Doors: 5:00 pm / Show: 6:00 pm All proceeds will be donated directly to Guitars4Vets. Guitars4Vets is a nonprofit founded in 2007 that provides free guitar lessons and a free guitar to veterans living with PTSD and other service-related trauma. The program started in Milwaukee after a guitar instructor and a Vietnam-era Marine veteran discovered music helped with healing, and it has grown to more than 110 chapters in over 40 states, plus remote options. Veterans, typically referred by VA medical staff or a Vet center, complete 10 weeks of one-on-one lessons with volunteer instructors and receive a free acoustic guitar, accessories, and a method book upon graduation. To date, Guitars4Vets reports giving more than 80,000 lessons and over 8,000 guitars to veterans. The organization emphasizes the mental health benefits of learning music. A study cited by Military.com found a 21% improvement in PTSD symptoms and a 27% decrease in depression symptoms among participants. In support of Veteran’s Day, Chaotic Order Entertainment seeks to raise awareness for veterans living with PTSD, and plans to donate all proceeds to the Butler, PA chapter of G4V. Representatives of G4V will be in attendance for the entirety of the event to provide more information and answer any questions regarding their program. This Event Is All Ages

EmBody: The ReSanctification of Black & Brown Queerness

Three Stories- Peirce Theater

937 Liberty Ave · Pittsburgh

Arts & Community: BurlesqueArts & Community: Fashion

EmBody: The ReSanctification of Black & Brown Queerness is a multidisciplinary performance art experience intended to restore the understanding that Queer and Trans bodies, stories, sensuality, and identities are Sacred. Deep in our ancestral memory, across cultures, Queer and Transgender people held revered roles as spiritual teachers, healers, shamans, and bridges between the physical and spiritual realms. Yet today, members of BIPOC & LGBTQIA+ communities continue to be demonized, devalued, and erased. Through poetry, live vocals, instrumental music, healing rituals, and choreography spanning multiple movement styles, EmBody follows the journey of a Divine Queer Soul as they enter the world and navigate the spirals of reality. Exploring ancestral veneration, decolonization, identity, community, death, and rebirth, we breathe new life into the Queer origin story. Be transported to the past present and future of Black and Brown performance art, and leave EmBodying a your own divinity.

Orpheus & Eurydice

Byham Theater

101 6th St · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$10-$195
Arts & Community: OperaArts & Community: Theater

After the death of his beloved Eurydice, Orpheus vows to plunge into the very depths of the Underworld itself to bring her back. Moved by Orpheus’s passion, Amore (Cupid) appears and agrees to aid him in the rescue of his wife so long as he does not look at her until they return to the land of the living again. With the help of the spirits of the Underworld, Orpheus finds Eurydice in Elysium. But as he guides her to the surface, he knows he cannot look back. Eurydice believes this means he does not love her, and she refuses to take another step until he looks her way. So he does… but this classic tale may not end the way you’ve seen before! Based on the same Greek myth that inspired the Broadway hit Hadestown, Christoph Willibald Gluck’s original 1774 score is enhanced by Hector Berlioz’s 1859 re-arrangement, making this a story that has only been enriched over the centuries. These performances are sponsored in part by The Gailliot Fund.

Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre (PBT)’s Pointe in Time fundraiser is a top 10 annual event that brings over 400 arts patrons together in support of PBT’s mainstage programming, arts education in schools and community centers, classes for individuals with disabilities, and funding for its Bridge Scholarship program. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

7:30 PM – 8:30 PM

Ten Evenings: Min Jin Lee

Carnegie Music Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh · Oakland

Get tickets$30.94 to $42.14
Arts & Community: LectureArts & Community: Literary

At last, the National Book Award finalist and NYT bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic: Min Jin Lee has written a masterpiece by turns sweeping and intimate, one that reckons with ambition and moderation, lust and loyalty, personal dreams and familial duty. In schools and churches, hotel rooms and nail salons, law firms and fried-fish shops; in cramped, dingy apartments and luxury, gated communities, the men, women, and children in American Hagwon struggle to find satisfaction and meaning in a world that seems to grow less forgiving with each passing year. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children—Bo, DH, and Mido—find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John’s oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis. Desperately striving to regain their footing, they leave Seoul for Sydney and eventually settle in Southern California—where new vistas of opportunity open up for the children as their parents, strangers in a strange land, must adjust to a new life in which their experience and education mean little, and they set their sights on whatever it takes to provide for their children’s futures. The Kohs, their friends, relatives, and even their foes move in and out of each other’s lives as they navigate new courses across the years, always nursing the almost all-consuming faith that education will lead the next generation to success and security. In American Hagwon, Min Jin Lee has crafted an unforgettable, panoramic novel where the smallest of gestures can have enormous repercussions, where the bonds of family and of memory twist and fray but rarely break, and where willful self-sacrifice—for the benefit of loved ones and even strangers—is a kind of prayer. Min Jin Lee is the author of the novels Free Food for Millionaires and Pachinko, a finalist for the National Book Award, runner-up for the Dayton Literary Peace Prize, and a New York Times “100 Best Books of the Century.” Lee is the 2024 recipient of The Fitzgerald Prize for Literary Excellence. From South Korea, Lee has received the Manhae Grand Prize for Literature, the Bucheon Diaspora Literary Award, and the Samsung Happiness for Tomorrow Award for Creativity. She is the recipient of fellowships in Fiction from the Guggenheim Foundation, the Radcliffe Institute of Advanced Study at Harvard, and the New York Foundation for the Arts. Lee is an inductee of the New York Foundation for the Arts Hall of Fame and the New York State Writers Hall of Fame. Lee served as the Editor of Best American Short Stories 2023. Lee’s essays and criticism have appeared in numerous publications, including The New York Times, The New Yorker, The New York Review of Books, Wall Street Journal, Travel & Leisure, Conde Nast Traveler, Vogue, and The Times of London. She is a Writer-in-Residence at Amherst College.

DBT Therapy Group

Online

Get ticketsFree
Arts & Community: Community

A skills-based DBT group for adults working on emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Dialectical Behavior Therapy teaches concrete tools for managing intense emotions, sitting with discomfort without acting on it, and communicating needs in relationships without escalating conflict. The group is facilitated by a licensed clinician at Darin King Counseling, a trauma-informed practice in downtown Pittsburgh. Sessions are structured around skills practice rather than open-ended discussion, so participants leave with something they can use that week. Group therapy is not a substitute for individual treatment, and a brief screening call is required before joining to make sure the group is a good fit. Space is limited. “That 70’s Rock Show” Doesn’t Just Play the Hits-They recreate the Electrifying Experience of the Greatest Decade in Rock History Coming to The Palace Theatre!

Palace Theatre

23 W. Otterman Street · Greensburg

Get tickets$33., $43., $48., and $75.
Music: Rock

Latshaw Productions Presents “That 70’s Rock Show” - a high-octane 70’s rock tribute that captures that lightning in a bottle, featuring Canada’s most elite musicians dedicated to delivering an authentic, electrifying live experience. This one-of-a-kind rock concert is coming to the Palace Theatre (21 W. Otterman, Greensburg, PA 15601) on Wed., Nov. 18th, 2026 at 7:30pm.Tickets are just $33., $43., $48., and $75. and can be purchased online at: www.westmorelandculturaltrust.org or by calling the ticket office at (724) 836-8000. The Palace Theatre is located at 21 W. Otterman, Greensburg, PA 15601. That 70’s Rock Show doesn’t just play the hits; they recreate the sonic architecture of the greatest decade in rock history. The band masterfully navigates the decade’s evolution, from the raw power of Led Zeppelin’s “Rock & Roll” and The Who’s “Baba O’Riley” to the sophisticated, jazzy precision of Steely Dan’s “Reelin’ In The Years.” Every performance is a deep dive into the 1970s’ most iconic sounds. Audiences will experience the soaring harmonies of the Eagles’ “Hotel California” and “Life In The Fast Lane,” the triple-threat guitar attack of The Doobie Brothers’ “China Grove,” and the legendary “talk-box” magic of Peter Frampton’s “Show Me The Way.” ### From Psychedelic Roots to Arena Anthems The magic of a That 70’s Rock Show performance lies in its ability to turn any venue into a sold-out stadium. The setlist is a non-stop barrage of “Main Event” moments that keep the energy at a fever pitch. Whether it’s the haunting atmosphere of Blue Oyster Cult’s “Don’t Fear The Reaper,” the high-definition pop of Electric Light Orchestra’s “Don’t Bring Me Down,” or the undeniable groove of Queen & David Bowie’s “Under Pressure,” the band delivers each track with the raw power of the original artists. The energy reaches its peak as the band dives into the anthemic drive of Boston’s “More Than A Feeling” and the soaring melodies of Journey’s “Any Way You Want It.” By the time the crowd is singing along to Fleetwood Mac’s “Go Your Own Way” and The Police’s “Message In A Bottle,” it becomes clear why this music remains the gold standard of the industry. That 70’s Rock Show is your ticket back to the greatest decade in rock music.

Orpheus & Eurydice

Byham Theater

101 6th St · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$10-$195
Arts & Community: OperaArts & Community: Theater

After the death of his beloved Eurydice, Orpheus vows to plunge into the very depths of the Underworld itself to bring her back. Moved by Orpheus’s passion, Amore (Cupid) appears and agrees to aid him in the rescue of his wife so long as he does not look at her until they return to the land of the living again. With the help of the spirits of the Underworld, Orpheus finds Eurydice in Elysium. But as he guides her to the surface, he knows he cannot look back. Eurydice believes this means he does not love her, and she refuses to take another step until he looks her way. So he does… but this classic tale may not end the way you’ve seen before! Based on the same Greek myth that inspired the Broadway hit Hadestown, Christoph Willibald Gluck’s original 1774 score is enhanced by Hector Berlioz’s 1859 re-arrangement, making this a story that has only been enriched over the centuries. These performances are sponsored in part by The Gailliot Fund.

SUBCINEMA Presents REMOTE CONTROL

Lost Lizard Video

5310 Butler Street · Pittsburgh · Lawrenceville

Get ticketsFREE
Arts & Community: Screen

Join us for a dead media presentation of Jeff Lieberman's sci-fi satire REMOTE CONTROL (1988). Presented on VHS and Projected on EIKI Video. From the filmmaker behind SQUIRM (1976) and BLUE SUNSHINE (1977) comes the criminally obscure REMOTE CONTROL. When a local video store receives a VHS tape of a popular 1950s science fiction film, rental clerk Cosmo realizes that the video is brainwashing his customers and causing them to commit ghastly murders. Convinced that the video is created by aliens hell-bent on destroying the earth, Cosmo and his friends must uncover the conspiracy behind this videotape before it's too late. Starring Kevin Dillon and Jennifer Tilly, REMOTE CONTROL is a unique and subversive tale about the dangers of abject media consumption and its effects on society. Offbeat yet provocative. The way only writer and director Jeff Lieberman can be. Presented on VHS and projected on a vintage EIKI LC-330 Video Projector. MATURE AUDIENCES ONLY. Doors open at 7:30 PM. Show starts at 8:00 PM. FREE & BYOB. SEATING IS LIMITED. RSVP REQUIRED.

1:00 PM

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Resonance Works: The Little Prince (Children’s Opera)

Andrew Carnegie Free Library & Music Hall

300 Beechwood Avenue · Carnegie

Get tickets$30-60 (Senior & Student prices are different price points)
Arts & Community: KidstuffArts & Community: Opera

Back by popular demand, Resonance Works revives its beloved production of The Little Prince, Rachel Portman's enchanting opera for all ages, based on Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's timeless story about a young prince who has been traveling the universe in search of what is most important in life, learning truths about love, friendship, and the importance of seeing with the heart. Our revival of this celebrated production by acclaimed stage director Keturah Stickann stars young artist Hudson Vasquez Schmitt as The Little Prince, with Daniel Teadt as The Pilot, Timothi Williams and Loghan Bazan as The Fox, Robert Frankenberry as The Snake and The Vain Man, Zuly Inirio as The Water, Yazid Gray as The Businessman, Brad Smoak as The King, Adrianna Cleveland as The Rose, and Holden Seward as The Drunkard. The Pittsburgh Youth Chorus are the chorus of birds and stars that support the Prince along his journey.

7:00 PM

Orpheus & Eurydice

Byham Theater

101 6th St · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$10-$195
Arts & Community: OperaArts & Community: Theater

After the death of his beloved Eurydice, Orpheus vows to plunge into the very depths of the Underworld itself to bring her back. Moved by Orpheus’s passion, Amore (Cupid) appears and agrees to aid him in the rescue of his wife so long as he does not look at her until they return to the land of the living again. With the help of the spirits of the Underworld, Orpheus finds Eurydice in Elysium. But as he guides her to the surface, he knows he cannot look back. Eurydice believes this means he does not love her, and she refuses to take another step until he looks her way. So he does… but this classic tale may not end the way you’ve seen before! Based on the same Greek myth that inspired the Broadway hit Hadestown, Christoph Willibald Gluck’s original 1774 score is enhanced by Hector Berlioz’s 1859 re-arrangement, making this a story that has only been enriched over the centuries. These performances are sponsored in part by The Gailliot Fund.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

And a Buoy by Eli Plummer is a staged reading about a father, a son, and a bond buoyed through the changing tides of time. Set entirely on a cuddy boat off the coast of Maine, the story anchors Sean and his son, Aaron, during their annual fishing trips. Words & Pictures: Elizabeth Acevedo

Carnegie Library Lecture Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh · Downtown

Get ticketsFree
Arts & Community: KidstuffArts & Community: Lecture

From National Book Award-winning, New York Times-bestselling author and renowned poet Elizabeth Acevedo comes a white-knuckle journey to self-understanding and doing the right thing, no matter the cost. Lil is anything but small. She’s rebellious, she’s loyal; she’s figuring out what kind of good person she wants to be, or if she wants to be a good person at all. But more than anything? Lil wants to be free. When her instinct for freedom leads to another stay in D.C. juvenile detention, Lil knows she’s lucky to just be on probation. But judgment, guilt, and an ankle monitor weigh heavily on her, and she can’t shake that pinned-down feeling. The only person who might understand is her big brother, Aldwin. Except he’s more distant now than just the hundred miles from his college. Something’s been off with him for several months, but only Lil seems to realize how important it is to get to him. As her court hearing ticks closer, a question looms over Lil as the missed phone calls and strange texts from her brother pile will she stay put, or put her future freedom on the line? Elizabeth Acevedo is the New York Times-bestselling author of The Poet X, which won the National Book Award for Young People’s Literature, the Michael L. Printz Award, the Pura Belpré Award, the Carnegie Medal, the Boston Globe–Horn Book Award, and the Walter Award. She is also the author of With the Fire on High—which was named a best book of the year by the New York Public Library, NPR, Publishers Weekly, and School Library Journal—and Clap When You Land, which was a Boston Globe–Horn Book Honor book and a Kirkus Prize finalist. She holds a BA in Performing Arts from The George Washington University and an MFA in Creative Writing from the University of Maryland. Acevedo has been a fellow of Cave Canem and Cantomundo, and a participant in the Callaloo Writer’s Workshops. She is a National Poetry Slam Champion, and resides in Washington, DC, with her family.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

WHAT SLEEPS BENEATH & SUBCINEMA Present THE HEAD

Poetry Lounge

313 North Ave. · Pittsburgh · Millvale

Get ticketsFREE
Arts & Community: Screen

Join SUBCINEMA and WHAT SLEEPS BENEATH for a special screening of the West German 1959 chiller THE HEAD (Die Nackte und der Satan, lit. "The Naked Woman and Satan"). Directed by Victor Trivas and photographed by Georg Krause (PATHS OF GLORY), this sci-fi horror was banned in Finland and sparked protests and police intervention in screenings in Austria. Michel Simon stars as Dr. Abel, whose new serum can keep a dog's disembodied head alive. When Abel suffers a fatal heart attack, his sinister assistant uses the formula to preserve the doctor's own severed head long enough to help transplant the head of a hunchbacked nurse onto the body of an exotic dancer. Long absent from the English-language market, THE HEAD has been called both a "thriller of the lowest quality" and an "unusually large success." We call it a real...head-turner.

7:30 PM – 8:30 PM

Ten Evenings: Nicholas Boggs

Carnegie Music Hall

4400 Forbes Avenue · Pittsburgh · Oakland

Get tickets$30.94 to $47.74
Arts & Community: LectureArts & Community: Literary

Drawing on new archival material, original research, and interviews, this spellbinding book is the first major biography of James Baldwin in three decades, revealing how profoundly his personal relationships shaped his life and work. Baldwin: A Love Story, the first major biography of James Baldwin in three decades, reveals how profoundly the writer’s personal relationships shaped his life and work. Drawing on newly uncovered archival material and original research and interviews, this spellbinding book tells the overlapping stories of Baldwin’s most sustaining intimate and artistic relationships: with his mentor, the Black American painter Beauford Delaney; with his lover and muse, the Swiss painter Lucien Happersberger; and with his collaborators, the famed Turkish actor Engin Cezzar and the iconoclastic French artist Yoran Cazac, whose long-overlooked significance as Baldwin’s last great love is explored in these pages for the first time. Nicholas Boggs shows how Baldwin drew on all the complex forces within these relationships—geographical, cultural, political, artistic, and erotic—and alchemized them into novels, essays, and plays that speak truth to power and had an indelible impact on the civil rights movement and on Black and queer literary history. Richly immersive, Baldwin: A Love Story follows the writer’s creative journey between Harlem, Paris, Switzerland, the southern United States, Istanbul, Africa, the South of France, and beyond. In so doing, it magnifies our understanding of the public and private lives of one of the major literary figures of the twentieth century, whose contributions only continue to grow in influence. Nicholas Boggs was an undergraduate when he discovered James Baldwin’s out-of-print children’s book, Little Man, Little Man: A Story of Childhood, in the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library. After he tracked down its illustrator, the French artist Yoran Cazac, he went on to coedit an acclaimed new edition of the book in 2018. His writing has also been anthologized in The Cambridge Companion to James Baldwin, James Baldwin Now, and Speculative Light: The Arts of Beauford Delaney and James Baldwin. He is the recipient of a 2023 Whiting Creative Nonfiction Grant and fellowships from the National Endowment for the Humanities, the Beinecke Library and Gilder Lehrman Center at Yale, the Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence Program, and the National Humanities Center, as well as residencies at Yaddo and MacDowell. He received his BA in English from Yale, his MFA in creative writing from American University, and his PhD in English from Columbia. Born and raised in Washington, DC, he lives in Brooklyn, New York.

1:00 PM

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

5:30 PM – 7:30 PM

Remind Me, My Dream

Kelly Strayhorn Theater

5941 Penn Ave · Pittsburgh · East Liberty

Get tickets$0 to %25
Arts & Community: Community

Seventeen AAPI artists from JADED use the creative process to explore layered identities and stories, while making space for dreams, grief, and connection. Through painting, sculpture, sound, film, wood, glass, and textiles, the artists reflect on messages held in their bodies, personal histories, and memories. The exhibition’s opening reception includes a Kintsugi Grief Bowls workshop with artist Kiyomi Knox, which uses the Japanese practice of repairing broken pottery with gold to symbolize the beauty that can exist in brokenness. Performing artist Arieux meditates on death, loss, and grief with a procession inspired by the ancient Chinese profession of corpse walkers. Remind Me, My Dream features works by Arieux, Anne Chen, Shimul Chowdhury, Sara Dtantirojanarat, Eriko Hattori, Sarah Khadraoui, Kiyomi Knox, Jules Lee, Justin Lin, Arthur Lindsay, Brent Nakamoto, Quartz/Court, Kimberly Rooney 高小荣, SEONI, Becky Sungja Kim, Zim Syed, and Zoyakeko. Led by women and non-binary artists, JADED is Pittsburgh’s first AAPI artist collective celebrating AAPI art & culture in Pittsburgh. Remind Me, My Dream is curated by Sara Tang in partnership with JADED and commissioned by KST in conjunction with Maree ReMalia’s WITH OURSELVES, WITH EACH OTHER.

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

1:00 PM

Data Sculpture: From Virtual to Bronze a solo exhibition by Digital Pioneer Paul Higham

Eberle Studios & Gallery

229 E. 9'th Ave · Homestead

Free
Arts & Community: Visual Art

Eberle Gallery is pleased to present DATA SCULTPURE, New Works by Paul Higham. As an early pioneer of digital sculpture and computational art Higham revisits concepts of encryption, retrieval and corruption through data visualization. Creating and manifesting sculptures from data and pure code. In one of the featured new works titled ‘NiKe’, he synthesizes scans of Nike and the Winged Victory of Samothrace with coding to produce emergent outcomes. The 3D printed form references remote data acquisition and agency in both ancient and modern indices. For example, Nike was sent from the hand of Athena, flown in service as an agent, a spy, a precursor to surveillance at a distance such as flock and drone technology of today. Opening Saturday Sept 12, 2026 from 6-9 PM at Eberle Studio Gallery, DATA SCULPTURE, New Works reactivate Higham’s early concepts bringing them into the present moment – reflecting on AI and the commodification of information within a broader technological landscape resonating with renewed relevance in today’s world. The Gallery is Open every Sat and Sun 1pm - 5pm through til Oct 18th

Musiq Soulchild

City Winery Pittsburgh

1627 Smallman Street · Pittsburgh

Get tickets$84.00
Music: Other Music

City Winery Pittsburgh presents Musiq Soulchild live on December 27th, 28th, and 30th as part of a six show series! Musiq Soulchild returns to Pittsburgh for an extended run of intimate performances at City Winery this December, featuring six shows across three nights. Join us for a special evening of soulful vocals, timeless R&B, and the unmistakable artistry that made Musiq one of the defining voices of his generation. Raised on the sounds of Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, and Donny Hathaway, Musiq Soulchild emerged from Philadelphia’s street music scene to help lead the neo-soul movement into the mainstream. His groundbreaking sound earned him 13 Grammy nominations, millions of albums sold worldwide, and recognition from Billboard, BET, Soul Train, ASCAP, and BMI. Known for his smooth delivery, emotional honesty, and magnetic live performances, Musiq continues to captivate audiences with fan favorites and deep cuts alike. Experience these special multi-night performances in the warm, intimate atmosphere of City Winery, complete with exceptional wine, dining, and live entertainment. Raised on the sounds of Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, and Donny Hathaway, Musiq Soulchild emerged from Philadelphia’s street music scene to help lead the neo-soul movement into the mainstream. His groundbreaking sound earned him 13 Grammy nominations, millions of albums sold worldwide, and recognition from Billboard, BET, Soul Train, ASCAP, and BMI. Known for his smooth delivery, emotional honesty, and magnetic live performances, Musiq continues to captivate audiences with fan favorites and deep cuts alike. Experience these special multi-night performances in the warm, intimate atmosphere of City Winery, complete with exceptional wine, dining, and live entertainment.
